name: Political Identity Test
tagline: See where you stand on the economic and social axes.
intro: Politics is about more than left and right. This test places your views on two separate axes: an economic axis, from state-led to market-led, and a social axis, from personal freedom to order and tradition. Rate 100 short policy statements; there are no right or wrong answers. In about five minutes you see where you stand and which broad political position fits you best.
seoTitle: Political Identity Test – Find your political position
seoDescription: Where do you stand politically? Take this free 5-minute test on economic and social views and see your position on a two-axis political map.

economic.name: Economic axis
economic.short: Whether you prefer the state or the free market to shape the economy (higher = more market-oriented).
economic.low: Your answers lean towards the economic left. You tend to see an active role for the state in reducing inequality, providing public services and protecting workers. You likely value solidarity, social security and public ownership of key services. People with this view often stress fairness and shared responsibility. To sharpen your thinking, explore how policies you support are funded and what trade-offs they involve, and read a well-argued market-oriented perspective to test your reasoning.
economic.mid: Your answers place you near the economic centre. You probably see value in both markets and government: free enterprise to create prosperity, and public policies to provide security and fairness. Your views may differ from issue to issue, which reflects a pragmatic approach. To understand your position better, notice which topics pull you left and which pull you right, and look at evidence from different countries on what works in practice.
economic.high: Your answers lean towards the economic right. You tend to favour free markets, lower taxes, private enterprise and personal responsibility, with a limited role for the state in the economy. People with this view often stress efficiency, choice and the link between effort and reward. To sharpen your thinking, consider how market-based policies affect people with fewer opportunities, and read a well-argued state-oriented perspective to test your reasoning.

social.name: Social axis
social.short: Whether you prioritise individual freedom or social order and tradition (higher = more order-oriented).
social.low: Your answers lean towards the libertarian side of the social axis. You tend to value personal freedom, privacy and self-determination, and you are wary of the state regulating private life or expanding its powers. People with this view often stress tolerance, diversity and individual rights. To sharpen your thinking, consider situations where freedoms may conflict with safety or with each other, and explore arguments for shared norms and institutions.
social.mid: Your answers place you near the centre of the social axis. You probably value both individual freedom and a certain degree of order, security and shared norms. Your views likely depend on the specific issue, such as drugs, policing or immigration. This balanced position can help you understand people on both sides. Reflect on which values matter most to you when freedom and order clash, and why.
social.high: Your answers lean towards the order-oriented side of the social axis. You tend to value security, tradition, shared norms and respect for authority, and you accept that the state may limit some freedoms to protect society. People with this view often stress stability, community and continuity. To sharpen your thinking, consider how rules affect minorities and dissenters, and explore arguments for individual liberty and privacy.

summary: Your answers place you on two independent axes: economic views (state-led versus market-led) and social views (personal freedom versus order and tradition). The combination determines your overall political position. No position is better or worse than another; this result simply describes your current views and is not linked to any party or politician.

left_libertarian.name: Left-libertarian
left_libertarian.text: Your answers combine left-leaning economic views with a strong emphasis on personal freedom. You likely support public services, social security and efforts to reduce inequality, while wanting the state to stay out of people's private lives. Values such as equality, tolerance, diversity and self-determination are probably important to you. In Europe, this combination is found among various green, social-liberal and progressive movements. Supporters see it as a way to combine fairness with freedom; critics question its costs or its view of tradition. Like every position, it involves trade-offs worth exploring with an open mind.

left_authoritarian.name: Left-communitarian
left_authoritarian.text: Your answers combine left-leaning economic views with a preference for social order and shared norms. You likely support a strong state role in the economy, solidarity and protection of workers, while also valuing security, community and clear rules. Many people across Europe hold this mix, emphasising both economic fairness and social cohesion. Supporters see it as protecting communities against both market insecurity and social disruption; critics question the limits it may place on markets or on individual freedom. Like every position, it involves trade-offs worth exploring with an open mind.

right_libertarian.name: Right-libertarian
right_libertarian.text: Your answers combine market-oriented economic views with a strong emphasis on personal freedom. You likely favour free enterprise, lower taxes and limited government, both in the economy and in private life. Individual responsibility, choice and self-reliance are probably central values for you. In Europe, this combination is often associated with classical liberal thinking. Supporters see it as the most consistent defence of liberty and prosperity; critics question how it handles inequality and shared public needs. Like every position, it involves trade-offs worth exploring with an open mind.

right_authoritarian.name: Right-conservative
right_authoritarian.text: Your answers combine market-oriented economic views with a preference for social order and tradition. You likely favour enterprise, personal responsibility and limited economic intervention, while valuing security, national identity, family and respect for institutions. Continuity and a sense of belonging probably matter to you. In Europe, this combination is associated with various conservative traditions. Supporters see it as balancing economic freedom with stable communities and shared values; critics question its effect on minorities or on economic equality. Like every position, it involves trade-offs worth exploring with an open mind.

centrist.name: Centrist
centrist.text: Your answers place you close to the middle on both the economic and the social axis. You probably judge issues one by one rather than following a single ideology, combining elements of both market and state, freedom and order. Pragmatism, compromise and evidence about what works are likely important to you. Many Europeans hold moderate views like these. Supporters see centrism as balanced and realistic; critics sometimes see it as lacking a clear direction. Your result may also reflect mixed or still-developing views, which is perfectly normal.
